notes:
This leaf has no author page number at its head and has later foliation 81 at the lower left. It is 22 main baseline rows, including four displays, plus the interlinear insertions (Zar) and base. No diagram or drawing is present. The author continues the arithmetic case: splitting of extension (13) is tied to vanishing of the previously named class and a global uniformizer along g(S); he says the condition is always locally satisfied in the Zariski sense and sufficient also outside the arithmetic case. He distinguishes splittings from choices of a basis of J_i/J_i^2, with indeterminacy G_m(S), from all sections of (13), with indeterminacy H^1(S,T). He writes Kummer exact sequences, passes to the inverse limit (21), and concludes H^1(S,T) is isomorphic to the completion of G_m(S) when the third term vanishes in the arithmetic case. These are the page's statements. The first reader performed no independent mathematical check; the later conditional calculation 082-N1 is recorded separately below and in check_events. Read the whole page once and both full-resolution halves once, comparing every word, abbreviation, accent, symbol, index, arrow and punctuation with both witnesses. Rechecked all four cancellations and both insertions. Each C/H word difference and each C doubt proposed for resolution has a saved crop; all other open places were cropped once. No region was re-cropped after decision. The (Zar) curve is an insertion leader, not cancellation of sur; base replaces section only. The quotation marks are ordinary doubles. The first class-equals-zero formula has extra retraced strokes and retains gamma/xi doubt; the later Quand gamma_i=0 is resolved separately by blind adjudication. Si l'on is also compressed and left doubtful. The first Kummer link has a small terminal hook, while the initial link in (21) is flat; the different readings are based on their ink, not on an exactness convention. The live first Kummer group is literally G_m(S)_n, and its endpoint is literally 1. H's quotient replacement is expressly editorial and is not imported into the text. The crowded end of (21) reaches the paper edge; a probable question mark is retained under doubt without an unsupported preceding arrow or completed endpoint. Cancelled H^0(S)_n stays doubtful. The cancelled label is preferably (21), but parts of its digits remain covered by hatching, so that label also retains explicit doubt. Neither the connected final return of privilégiés nor the final bottom formula supplies a separate terminal stop. No OCR, external research, unrelated page inputs or TeX compilation was used.

Actual check 082-N1 (conditional finite-group calculation): if an abelian group A is killed by an integer e, a coherent family a_n in A[n] for the transition maps A[mn]→A[n], a↦ma, satisfies a_n=e a_{en}=0. Hence its Tate inverse limit is zero. This verifies the algebraic vanishing when the relevant Picard torsion has bounded exponent; it does not establish the arithmetic finiteness hypothesis or the exactness of the preceding inverse-limit sequence. The written terminal 1 is retained as a group identity convention, without replacing it by the additive endpoint 0.

Blind-reading adjudication corrects the first paragraph-transition reading: the next paragraph begins Quand gamma_i=0, not Bien plus. Q/u/a/n/d and the two equality strokes followed by zero are visible. The deep descending stem/right branch of gamma matches the clearer class notation on 081 and 085, whereas the earlier formula on this leaf still has extra retraced strokes and retains gamma/xi doubt. This is a notation comparison, not a proof of the splitting claim. The cancelled (21) label and final cancelled G_m now retain explicit doubt because hatching obscures parts of their strokes. All 17 differing boxes were inspected; crop-boundary truncations did not remove complete source words.

check_events.outcome: For bounded-exponent abelian A, proved lim_n A[n]=0 with multiplication transition maps: if eA=0, coherence gives a_n=e a_en=0. Does not establish the Picard-group hypothesis or inverse-limit exactness.
